blocks.orig: Saadani is a national park that is often overlooked. Its location is special because it is on the coast, because it is the only national park where you can combine an adventure safari with a relaxing stay at beautiful white beaches with many palm trees. It is allowing you to observe wildlife in a unique environment. Saadani is the only national park on the coast of East Africa. It is where the beach meets the bush – the only wildlife sanctuary in East Africa to boast an Indian Ocean beachfront.
blocks.html: Saadani is a national park that many travellers pass by. Its setting on the coast makes it special: it is the only national park where an adventurous safari can be paired with a relaxed stay on lovely white, palm-fringed beaches, letting you watch wildlife in a truly unusual environment. No other national park in East Africa sits on the coast. Here the beach meets the bush, in the only wildlife sanctuary in East Africa with a beachfront on the Indian Ocean.

blocks.orig: It as well possesses all the attributes that make Tanzania’s tropical coastline and islands very popular with European sun-worshipers. Yet it is also the one place where those idle hours of sunbathing might be interrupted by an elephant strolling past. Or a lion coming to drink at the nearby waterhole! It offers a variety of landscapes: mangroves, large coral reefs, sea and beach with many palm trees, savannah and cotton fields.
blocks.html: The park also has everything that makes Tanzania’s tropical coast and islands such a draw for European sun-seekers. At the same time, it is the one spot where a lazy hour of sunbathing might be interrupted by an elephant wandering past, or a lion arriving for a drink at the waterhole nearby. The scenery is varied too: mangroves, extensive coral reefs, sea and palm-lined beach, savannah and cotton fields.

blocks.orig: Wildlife in Saadani national park includes four of the Big Five. Although it is very hard to spot them, because the numbers are low and the animals are usually hiding. Because this park is located next to the local villages and animals try to avoid interaction with local people. As they see them as their enemies.
blocks.html: Four of the Big Five live in Saadani national park, though spotting them is far from easy, as numbers are low and the animals tend to stay hidden. The park borders local villages, and the wildlife does its best to avoid contact with people, whom it regards as a threat.

blocks.orig: You can also find a population of Masai giraffes. And you find Lichtenstein’s hartebeest, common waterbucks and bohor reedbucks, blue wildebeests, common and red duikers, Dik-Diks. Others are yellow baboons, vervet and blue sykes monkeys as well as Colobus and White-bearded emperor tamarin monkeys, mongooses, genets and porcupines. And also greater kudus, elands, sable antelopes, warthogs, hippos, crocodiles and nile monitors live in Saadani national park. African bush elephants, lions and leopards are a bit more shy here. But with a bit of luck you might spot them too! You can see herds of up to 30 elephants with increased frequency. And several lion prides are inhabitants, together with leopards, spotted hyenas and black-backed jackals.
blocks.html: There is a population of Masai giraffes here as well. You will also find Lichtenstein’s hartebeest, common waterbucks and bohor reedbucks, blue wildebeests, common and red duikers and Dik-Diks. Then there are yellow baboons, vervet and blue sykes monkeys, plus Colobus and White-bearded emperor tamarin monkeys, mongooses, genets and porcupines. Greater kudus, elands, sable antelopes, warthogs, hippos, crocodiles and nile monitors call Saadani national park home too. African bush elephants, lions and leopards keep a lower profile in this park, but with a little luck you may see them as well. Herds of as many as 30 elephants are being seen more and more often, and several lion prides live here alongside leopards, spotted hyenas and black-backed jackals.

blocks.orig: Since 2005, the protected area is considered a Lion Conservation Unit. The Wami River is home to the beautiful mangrove kingfisher and lesser flamingo. And the beaches form one of the last major green turtle breeding sites on mainland Tanzania.
blocks.html: The protected area has been recognised as a Lion Conservation Unit since 2005. Along the Wami River you can find the beautiful mangrove kingfisher and the lesser flamingo, while the beaches are among the last important breeding grounds for green turtles on mainland Tanzania.

blocks.orig: In Saadani National Park you can go on a boat safari on the mangrove-lined Wami River, where you can see hippos, huge crocodiles and beautiful mangrove kingfisher and lesser flamingo.
blocks.html: A boat safari on the mangrove-fringed Wami River is one of the things to do in Saadani National Park; expect hippos, enormous crocodiles and the beautiful mangrove kingfisher and lesser flamingo.

blocks.orig: For another nice activity you can do here is a walking safari. Here you walk through the park with an armed ranger.
blocks.html: A walking safari is another pleasant option here: you cross the park on foot in the company of an armed ranger.

blocks.orig: Or visit Saadani fishing village, which lies within the reserve, where a collection of ruins pays testament to its 19th century heyday as a major trading port.
blocks.html: Alternatively, pay a visit to Saadani fishing village inside the reserve, where a cluster of ruins bears witness to its 19th century heyday as an important trading port.

blocks.orig: Off the coast of the national park is a sandbank which you can visit by boat to go snorkeling, swimming, relaxing and enjoying the tropical environment. The sandbank is only accessible during low tide, so your trip should happen during this time.
blocks.html: Just off the park's coast lies a sandbank that you can reach by boat for snorkelling, swimming, lazing about and soaking up the tropical setting. It only emerges at low tide, so the trip needs to be timed accordingly.

blocks.orig: Travel Tips from our experts about Saadani

My name is Wilfred and I am a guide in Saadani National Park for 9 years. Our guests mainly like this park due to its proximity to the ocean. This unique combination of beach holiday and exciting safari game drives is what they enjoy most as they find all in one location! The abundance of animals and boats tours make for unforgettable memories.
blocks.html: I am Wilfred, and I have guided in Saadani National Park for 9 years. What our guests like most about this park is how close it is to the ocean. Having a beach holiday and thrilling safari game drives rolled into a single location is the combination they enjoy most. The wealth of wildlife and the boat trips leave lasting memories.

blocks.orig: Best time to visit Saadani National Park
blocks.html: When to visit Saadani National Park

blocks.orig: The best time for watching wildlife in Saadani is after the rains, in January and February, and from June to August, when there is still plenty of water on the plains and wildlife stays within the park.
blocks.html: Wildlife watching in Saadani is at its best after the rains, during January and February and from June to August, when the plains still hold plenty of water and the animals remain inside the park.

blocks.orig: Avoid the rainy season in April-May and November.
blocks.html: Steer clear of the rainy season in April-May and November.

blocks.orig: Elephants bathing in the ocean. Lions and hyenas on the hunt. Numerous different species of monkeys swinging through the trees. Saadani National Park is home to many representatives of the African animal kingdom, although they can also hide well. Nevertheless, this park is an absolute highlight, as safari adventures and relaxation on the beach merge seamlessly.
blocks.html: Elephants taking a dip in the ocean. Lions and hyenas out hunting. Countless kinds of monkeys leaping through the trees. Many members of the African animal kingdom live in Saadani National Park, even if they are also good at staying out of sight. All the same, the park is a real highlight, because safari adventure and beach relaxation blend here without a seam.
